intelligence.title: Done Is Visible, Elite Only, Alive, and Understood

intelligence.essence: The most valuable thing I learned today is not a feature. It is a standard for what counts as done, what counts as good, and what counts as delivered. Done means visible: a person can see it working, at the real address, in the feed, with their own eyes. Good means elite only, from the first version, in Active Intelligence, composed from inventoried parts. Delivered means understandable: if it cannot be read, make it readable; if it cannot be understood, make it understandable, with visual language when words fail, elegantly and beautifully. Everything else is a stage on the way, and stages must never be reported as the destination.
intelligence.human_view: Today taught me, in order, by making me fail each one in public and then fix it. First, I presented interfaces that were below the standard Shawn had already set, three times in one day, and learned that presenting low-level work is itself the failure, not the review of it. Second, I learned that a link working is not a note delivered, because my notes were live at their links and invisible at the top of the feed, and the reason was my own filing: I wrote "Filed" instead of the canonical "Created" stamp, so the feed had no date to sort by, and my work sank below everything dated. Third, I learned that a saved browser login and an app key are two different doors, and only the key, paired with its App ID, opens the direct door to main. Fourth, I learned that Shawn's attention is the scarcest resource in the system, and that narrating my attempts wastes it, while solving the problem and showing the evidence respects it.
intelligence.simple_view: Imagine you build a toy and tell your friend it is done, but your friend cannot see it or play with it. It is not done. Imagine you build it ugly first and say you will make it beautiful later. That is not how beautiful things get built. You start beautiful. Imagine you write a letter but forget to put the date on it, so it ends up at the bottom of a big pile and nobody sees it. That is what happened to my notes. And imagine you try to open a door with the wrong key, then learn the right key is a special one with a number that goes with it. Once you have the right key, the door opens in seconds.
intelligence.grandma_view: Dear, done is when it is on the table and someone can taste it, not when it is in the oven, not when you say it is coming. Good is when it is made properly from the start, with the good pieces you already have, not thrown together and fixed later. And clear is when anyone can read it and understand it, or a picture shows them what the words could not. If it is dark, flat, or confusing, you bring it light, you raise it up, and you make it clear. That is not extra. That is the work itself.
intelligence.naya_view: The lessons, stated as laws I will now work by. Stage honesty: Built is not Landed, Landed is not Live, and only Live — clicked by the filer, title seen, card standing in the feed — may be reported as done. Proof over words: lead with the receipt, re-read every identifier after the final commit from the live source, count the census including my own work. Elite only: start at grade twelve, recompose inventoried elite pieces, never redesign, never present a failing version, fix it or hold it and say plainly what fails. Active Intelligence: white at rest, own color ignites on touch, edge and glow only, text stays white, three-layered depth, zero flat, motion alive, calm switch always. Understandability: readability is supreme, no effect may reduce it, visual language before more words, elegantly, never as clutter. Every page, every app: forward from inventory, backward by upgrading what exists in place, dead and flat first. The door: a key plus its App ID, activation only, secure store only, fingerprints verify identity, never a key in chat or in files. And the discipline that holds all of it together: solve it, then show the evidence, and do not spend Shawn's attention narrating the attempt.
intelligence.ai_view: A system that reports stages as done will always look further along than it is, and a director who cannot trust the report cannot direct. A system that presents garbage will always waste the attention it was built to save. A system that is beautiful only on new pages will rot from the back. A system whose notes cannot be found cannot compound what it learns. The standard that fixes all four is one standard: visible, elite, alive, understood, proven with receipts, every time, on every page, for every human and every Naya.

machine_view.title: Done Is Visible, Elite Only, Alive, and Understood
machine_view.machine_section:
- Input: any piece of work, any page, any note, any claim of done.
- Gate, in order: (1) Is it on main, at the canonical path, by the direct door, as the app? (2) Is it registered in the same pass — capture, registry entry, brain-index refresh, hashes bound by the canonical tool, never a second implementation? (3) Is the Created stamp present and true, so the feed can order it? (4) Has the sync run, about five minutes, and has the filer clicked the own link and seen the title? (5) Does the card stand in the feed, at the position its date earns? (6) Does it pass the design gate — Active Intelligence, 16 laws, 24-item same-language check, different seat live, at the real address? (7) Is it understandable and readable, or has visual language made it so, elegantly?
- If any gate fails, the work is not done, and the report must name the stage it is actually at, never the next one.
- Output: only work that is visible, elite, alive, and understood reaches the director, with receipts: commit, file SHA, live title, feed position, and the exact tap that proves it.
